For example, when Windows went to 64-bits, not everything was re-written and re-compiled. Many libraries and older application code would 'Thunk' to switch to the lower resolution mode. The code would run and do its thing, and then switch back to what the main program mode was.

Thunk'ing is avoided as much as possible because it is very time consuming. But it works and provides backwards compatibility.
